# /agree — refusal-first working agreement capture

Thin macro over the **already-coded** refusal gate. Do not re-implement the write rules here;
`tools.agree.write` owns them.

## Invocation

Arguments are passed positionally to the coded writer; do not build shell strings from feedback.

!`uv run python -m tools.agree.write $ARGUMENTS`

## The gate (refusal is the default)

- Adding requires `--because "<verbatim user feedback>"`. Missing, empty, or whitespace-only
  feedback is refused with exit 3. The value becomes the provenance stamp.
- `GOLDEN_APPROVE_HUMAN` is **not required**: agreements are not constitution-plane changes; the
  user directing the write is the ratification.
- `--retire <slug>` changes `status:` to `retired` in place and never deletes the entry. The file
  remains the audit trail.
- Agreements are committed and injected into every session. Never put secrets, tokens,
  credentials, or PII in `--because`.
- Agreements cover working style or methodology only. A project or architecture decision belongs
  in `docs/adr/`; link it with `Related:`, never restate it.

This makes a provenance stamp impossible to forget, not impossible to forge: a well-formed but
fabricated provenance still passes shape lint. Fabricating a user quote is nevertheless visible
and auditable in the git diff rather than a silent accident.

Example (human-run):

```sh
uv run python -m tools.agree.write capture-scope \
  --title "Capture scope" \
  --rule "Confirm the requested scope before expanding work." \
  --because "Please keep the implementation limited to the requested scope." \
  --related "[ADR-0002](../../docs/adr/0002-general-template-de-specialization.md)"
```
